svg.text: What to remember FIRST — the pre-interview ladder (memorize, then tell the story)
one-liner → framework → numbers → the ladder → entities → level bar
"Stateful WebSocket chat with durable inbox fan-out; media offloaded to S3; messages purged after 30 days."
Requirements (4 FR / 5 NFR) → Core entities (5) → API (WebSocket commands) → HLD (1 server, then break it) → Deep dives.
③ The numbers (cold-call them, in this order):
500 ms latency · ~2B users · 2M connections/server ⇒ ~1 000 servers · 100 msgs/user/day · 1 KB cap ⇒ 100 TB/day
30-day TTL · 100-row DynamoDB transaction ⇒ group ≤ 100 members · devices capped at 2–3
④ The routing ladder (with WHY, not just the verdict):
Kafka ✗ (50–100 KB/topic ⇒ TBs) → consistent hash ~ (correct, migration orchestration + hot servers) →
Redis Pub/Sub ✓ (thin fast-lane; durable messages+inbox is the source of truth).
⑤ Entities: User (peer) · Chat · ChatParticipant · Message · Inbox (+ Client for devices/presence)
the Inbox row-per-recipient is the single most important data-model idea in this problem
⑥ Where each level earns the offer (say the one that matches you):
mid = WebSockets + pub/sub + DB design, call out the challenges · senior = L4 LB + consistent hashing for STATEFUL services
staff = zoom into the fan-out + data-model trade-offs, bring a bigger toolkit, generalize on the statefulness insight.
